In [[functional analysis]], the '''Dixmier–Ng theorem''' is a characterization of when a [[normed space]] is in fact a [[Banach space#Dual space|dual Banach space]]. It was proven by Kung-fu Ng, who called it a variant of a theorem proven earlier by [[Jacques Dixmier]].<ref name=ng/><ref>{{citation
 | last = Dixmier | first = J. | author-link = Jacques Dixmier
 | date = December 1948
 | doi = 10.1215/s0012-7094-48-01595-6
 | issue = 4
 | journal = Duke Mathematical Journal
 | pages = 1057–1071
 | title = Sur un théorème de Banach
 | volume = 15}}</ref>

: '''Dixmier-Ng theorem.'''<ref name=ng>{{citation
 | last = Ng | first = Kung-fu
 | date = December 1971
 | doi = 10.7146/math.scand.a-11054
 | journal = Mathematica Scandinavica
 | pages = 279–280
 | title = On a theorem of Dixmier
 | volume = 29}}</ref> Let <math>X</math> be a normed space. The following are equivalent:
#  There exists a [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] [[Locally convex topological vector space|locally convex topology]] <math>\tau</math> on <math>X</math> so that the [[closed unit ball]], <math>\mathbf{B}_X</math>, of <math>X</math> is <math>\tau</math>-compact.
# There exists a Banach space <math>Y</math> so that <math>X</math> is isometrically isomorphic to the dual of <math>Y</math>.

That 2. implies 1. is an application of the [[Banach–Alaoglu theorem]], setting <math>\tau</math> to the [[Weak-* topology]]. That 1. implies 2. is an application of the [[Bipolar theorem]].

==Applications==
Let <math>M</math> be a [[pointed space|pointed]] [[metric space]] with distinguished point denoted <math>0_M</math>. The Dixmier-Ng Theorem is applied to show that the [[Lipschitz space]] <math>\text{Lip}_0(M)</math> of all real-valued [[Lipschitz function]]s from <math>M</math> to <math>\mathbb{R}</math> that vanish at <math>0_M</math> (endowed with the [[Lipschitz function|Lipschitz constant]] as norm) is a dual Banach space.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Godefroy | first1 = G.
 | last2 = Kalton | first2 = N. J.
 | doi = 10.4064/sm159-1-6
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Studia Mathematica
 | pages = 121–141
 | title = Lipschitz-free Banach spaces
 | volume = 159
 | year = 2003}}</ref>
